independent_computation.step_1_what_the_named_items_can_move: The scenario is named for exactly two items. Black Cleaver (S4) authors no damage instance at all: 'Carve' is armor reduction and 'Fervor' is movement speed. By S5/S6, armor reduction and penetration act only through the mitigation multiplier m(R) = 100/(100+R); they can change post-mitigation damage but can NEVER change an authored raw (pre-mitigation) amount. Therefore a change to a raw_damage leaf in this scenario cannot come from Black Cleaver.
independent_computation.step_2_bloodsong_is_the_only_raw_author: Bloodsong (S1/S2/S3) authors exactly two combat effects: (a) a Spellblade on-hit proc whose amount is 100% BASE AD (the wiki cache bolds '''base'''), physical, once per 1.5 s inside a 10 s window; (b) 'Expose Weakness', an 8% (melee) / 5% (ranged) increased-damage-taken debuff for 4 s. Bloodsong itself grants 0 AD and 0 AP.
independent_computation.step_3_rule_out_the_amp: observed ratio = 53.4 / 90.1 = 0.592675 (a 40.73% reduction; absolute delta 36.7). Expose Weakness can only move a number by a factor of 1.08 or 1.05 (or their reciprocals 0.9259 / 0.9524), and any composition of the two amp values (1.08·1.05 = 1.134, 1.08^n, 1.05^n) never lands on 0.5927 for integer n. So the change is NOT an amplifier-placement change.
independent_computation.step_4_rule_out_count_or_percentage_chan: 0.592675 is not any simple proc/tick-count ratio (1/2 = 0.5, 3/5 = 0.6, 2/3 = 0.667) nor any sourced percentage in either item (6%, 30%, 8%, 5%, 100%). The change is therefore a change of SCALING BASIS, not of a multiplier or of an event count.
independent_computation.step_5_the_only_wiki-legal_basis: S1 pins the Spellblade amount at 100% of BASE attack damage. Base AD is the growth-curve value of S7, base + growth·(L−1)·(0.7025 + 0.0175·(L−1)); it is always strictly less than total AD whenever the holder carries any bonus AD (Black Cleaver alone supplies 40 flat AD, S4/S8). The classic implementation error for a Spellblade is scaling on TOTAL AD instead, which over-states the proc by exactly the bonus AD; correcting it always produces a REDUCTION of the raw amount, which is the direction observed (90.1 -> 53.4, delta 36.7, i.e. the bonus AD the holder carries).

step_6_growth_curve_preimages.method: Solved base + growth·(L−1)·(0.7025 + 0.0175·(L−1)) over all 173 cached champions x levels 1..20 (S7) for each value.
step_6_growth_curve_preimages.note: Both values sit on the base-AD growth curve for SOME (champion, level), which is itself evidence that the leaf is an AD-basis quantity rather than a flat ability row (flat ability values in the cache are integers or .5 steps, and item AD is integral per S9).

independent_computation.step_7_consistency_test_on_the_old_value: If the old number were the correct base-AD proc and the new one the error, the new number would have to be a wiki-legal downgrade of base AD. There is none: Bloodsong offers no fractional multiplier, and the only alternative AD basis (bonus AD) can only take the values {0, 15, 25, 40} for a Black Cleaver build stage (S8/S9) — never 53.4. Conversely, if the new number is the corrected 100%-base-AD proc, the old number is explained as 100% of TOTAL AD (base + bonus AD = 53.4 + 36.7 = 90.1), i.e. the standard base-vs-total over-count. Exactly one of the two readings leaves the OTHER number explainable, and it is the reading in which the NEW value is correct.
independent_computation.conclusion: raw_damage for a Bloodsong Spellblade proc = 100% of the holder's BASE attack damage (S1/S3), a growth-curve value (S7) that excludes Black Cleaver's 40 flat AD. The post-change value 53.4 is consistent with that formula (it is an exact base-AD growth-curve value); the pre-change value 90.1 exceeds base AD by 36.7, i.e. by the holder's bonus AD, which is the signature of a total-AD over-count. Neither Black Cleaver's Carve (armor reduction, S4/S5/S6) nor Expose Weakness (8%/5%, S1/S3) can produce the observed 40.73% raw reduction, so no competing explanation survives.

limits_and_caveats: The scenario input tuple for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' (participants, per-participant levels, per-participant builds, roster order) is NOT inside the permitted evidence tree — it lives in tests/ or scripts/, which this runbook forbids. I therefore could not pin WHICH champion at WHICH level authors events[35], and so could not reproduce 53.4 digit-for-digit from a single closed form.

The verdict rests on (a) the sourced formula '100% base AD' (S1/S3), (b) the exclusion of every other mechanism the two named items own (S4/S5/S6), and (c) the asymmetry in step_7: the new value is explainable as base AD and leaves the old value explainable as total AD, whereas the reverse reading leaves the new value unexplainable by any cached number.

Residual risk: if events[35] is not the Bloodsong Spellblade proc but a health-path-dependent instance (e.g. a %-current-health term whose input moved because an earlier event changed), the ratio 0.5927 would carry no closed-form meaning and this analysis would not bind. That possibility cannot be excluded from data/ alone.

Cross-check attempted and negative: no (champion, level) in the cache has base AD 50.1, so '90.1 = base AD + Black Cleaver 40' is not literally realisable; the holder's bonus AD in this scenario is 36.7, which is consistent with a partial build stage plus adaptive-force rune AD rather than a completed Black Cleaver on the Bloodsong holder (a coupled roster can split the two items across participants).
